profile.headline: Staff Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
I am currently a software engineer at Google.

I worked for over 4 years as a software engineer at LiveRamp powering their real-time integrations systems.

Prior to this, I was a software engineer at Knewton working in the adaptive learning team. My primary responsibility was developing the models and software for Knewton's recommendation engine.

Previously, I worked as a research engineer at the Child Mind Institute in New York City developing software to process and analyze neuroimaging datasets, using techniques in signal processing, machine learning, and statistical analysis.

I completed my Master's degree in Electrical Engineering at Columbia University in New York City. There, I focused on methods and approaches in signal processing, machine learning, and computational neuroscience.

Prior to my graduate studies, I worked as a Principal Engineer at a startup engineering consulting firm in the Philadelphia area, OTW Technology, Inc. There I honed my skills in statistical analysis, firmware development, circuit design, GUI development, database and website maintenance, and client relations.

I graduated with my Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering from Villanova University in May of 2009, with a concentration in electronics and signal processing.  My senior capstone involved work on a custom electronic expressive guitar pedal operated by a varying capacitive pad.

In addition, I am a musician who composes, records, performs, and produces original and covered songs, particularly in guitar, banjo, djembe, tablas, and bass. I am also a distance running enthusiast and enjoy hiking, skiing, and rock climbing.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Built up the software, infrastructure, and tools for LiveRamp's realtime integration systems. This involved routine improvements and maintenance on systems handling web traffic on the order of 200k+ req/s.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Built educational products that adapt to each individual student. I was primarily developing software in Java and Python for the adaptive learning models and real-time recommendations.

positions.title: Research Engineer
positions.description: Developed the software to automate the preprocessing and analysis of very large-scale neuroimaging datasets. This included implementing novel signal processing, machine learning and statistical methods in Python and C/C++ as well as performing analyses on very large fRMI, MRI, DTI and EEG datasets using high performance computing infrastructures.

positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description: Worked for the summer as a contractor for the AFRL under the Repperger Research Intern Program. Project work consisted of developing computer-based models for automatically detecting and classifying various humans from aircraft-mounted cameras based on anthropometric differences. Experimented with techniques in computer vision, image processing, machine learning, biomechanics, control theory, and stochastic modeling.

positions.title: Principal Engineer
positions.description: Researched and developed products used by the military, automotive, and lighting industries.  Performed analog and digital circuit design, PCB layout and population, and firmware/software development for signal processing and controls theory.

positions.title: Electrical Engineer Intern
positions.description: Analyzed and revised various power system grids for large Biotech and Pharmaceutical facilities.  Work experience included heavy CAD work as well as short circuit analysis and arc flash simulations.  Implemented AutoCAD and SKM software tools.

positions.title: Electrical Engineer Intern
positions.description: Drafted and edited power system grids and components of large Biotech and Pharmaceutical development facilities using CAD.  Worked closely with chemical, mechanical and process engineers.  Involved extensive experience with AutoCAD and MicroStation software.

patents.title: LED Retrofit Luminaire Tubes
patents.description: An LED retrofit tube that has an outer body that is substantially a lens so as to enable light generated by LEDs and light reflected therewithin to pass through substantially the entire tube. The tube includes an extrusion to support a circuit board having light emitting diodes (LEDs) mounted thereto. The extrusion is located substantially with the lens. The circuit boards may include LEDs mounted on both sides to provide primary lighting and secondary lighting (backlighting). The extrusion may include grooves to allow the backlighting to pass therethrough. Rotational endcaps include an inner portion and an outer portion that can rotate with respect to one another to enable the tube to be rotated and the light dispersed therefrom to be focused.

patents.title: LED luminaires power supply
patents.description: An LED luminaires power supply that isolates dangerous line power from the LED luminaires. The power supply's footprint may enable retrofitting in existing lighting fixtures (e.g., replace ballast in florescent tube troffer). The power supply may individually power a plurality of LED luminaires based on power requirements of the individual LED luminaires. The power supply may receive and interpret TRIAC dimmer signals and/or other lighting protocol commands and provide dimming and/or other lighting scenarios to the LED luminaires. The power supply may include identification readers to read identification and/or power requirements for the LED luminaires being powered thereby (stored in luminaires or in adapters connected to luminaires). The LED luminaires driven by the power supply may include individual lighting fixtures (e.g., LED tubes, LED bulbs), a plurality of LED light arrays in a single light fixture (e.g., LED street lights, LED high hats), or some combination thereof.
